body: The decision to sack Sage was made on Sunday evening after Palace slumped to a 3-1 defeat against Liverpool. It was their fourth successive loss in the Premier League and left them bottom of the table for the first time since 2017.

Despite reports on Monday that Sage had been relieved of his post, he has yet to be officially sacked and it is understood that negotiations over compensation over his three-year contract are ongoing. However, Yannick Cahuzac’s sacking by Lens on Tuesday after they were embarrassed 9-1 by Como in a record-equalling Champions League defeat last week before losing 2-1 to Marseille in Ligue 1 has opened the possibility of a swift return to northern France.

articles.title: Jordon Hudson files lawsuit over shirtless video of Belichick that helped disclose romance
articles.summary: Age-gap relationship generated intense scrutiny. Hudson says clip invaded her privacy. Jordon Hudson is suing two Airbnb hosts over a Ring doorbell camera video of a bare-chested Bill Belichick.
body: Hudson, who went on to become a public presence by Belichick’s side, says in the lawsuit that the pair were keeping their romantic relationship private when they stayed at the Boston-area rental in the summer of 2023. However, the doorbell video – which showed a shirtless Belichick stepping out of the home – emerged that fall and soon made the rounds in the media.

Hudson wasn’t in the video, but she was later identified as the partner of the Super Bowl-winning head coach, who is almost 50 years her senior. Her lawsuit accuses the Airbnb hosts, Elise McDevitt and Craig Nolan, of leaking the footage and personal information about Hudson.

“These egregious violations of Ms Hudson’s privacy have, among other things, resulted in significant unwanted publicity and scrutiny of Ms Hudson and her relationship with Mr Belichick” and subjected her to ridicule, attorney Howard Cooper and colleagues wrote in a complaint filed on Friday in Massachusetts.
McDevitt, Nolan and Belichick have yet to respond publicly to the lawsuit.

articles.title: Formula 1 to finish season in Middle East
articles.summary: The 2026 Formula 1 season will conclude with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix as planned, with Italy's Imola circuit stood down as back-up for the races.
body: Formula 1 has told the Imola circuit in Italy that it will not be required as a back-up for the two end-of-season races in the Middle East.

The sport is pressing ahead with plans to hold the two events in Qatar on 27-29 November and Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates on 4-6 December, despite the ongoing conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran.
Imola had been asked to prepare for a potential grand prix on the Abu Dhabi dates if the two Middle Eastern races could not go ahead.
Imola was asked on Tuesday to stand down preparations - but F1 says that if the situation in the Middle East deteriorates it is still prepared to cancel the two races.

articles.title: Hot mics, Andreeva ‘diva’ drama and a stopgap finale at Indian Wells bail out the WTA | Tumaini Carayol
articles.summary: Finals have hit California desert after stormy few years and pre-tournament kerfuffle has added to the fun. Towards the end of a positive day for Mirra Andreeva, one of the brightest young stars of women’s tennis, the 19-year-old approached the broadcast cameras to dissect her excellent 6-4, 6-0…
body: This was an obvious reference to the kerfuffle on the eve of the tournament, when Jessica Pegula, usually known as one of the most congenial players on the tour, had been caught on a hot mic delivering a series of stinging criticisms about Andreeva in a private conversation with her coach. Pegula, who had just finished a practice set with an angsty Andreeva, described her rival as a “diva” who “needs to be humbled”. Her comments instantly spread to all corners of the internet.

On the court, women’s tennis is in the middle of one of its best eras in recent years. The depth at the top of the sport is so immense that every member of the current top 10 holds a grand slam or WTA 1000 title. Such is the strength of the tour, there was not even space in the WTA Finals, which pits the top eight players against each other, for the six-time grand slam champion Iga Swiatek, who finished No 9 and missed the event for the first time since 2019.

articles.title: Six Nations and Sanzaar face new battle with World Rugby in bid to scrap relegation
articles.summary: F10 unions fear financial loss if they play in second tier. Promotion/relegation set for 2030 Nations Championship. The Six Nations and Sanzaar are facing another battle with World Rugby over a desire from some unions to ensure that none of them can be relegated from the Nations Championship.
body: As reported last week by the Guardian, the 10 leading unions have set up a new company, F10, to run the Nations Championship and sell their broadcast and commercial rights for all competitions other than the World Cup, which remains the property of the global governing body, World Rugby.

The creation of F10 has led to concerns elsewhere in the sport that some of the 10 founding unions, particularly Wales and Italy, want to introduce guard rails protecting them from relegation to the second tier Nations Cup, which is run by World Rugby.

In another potential flashpoint there is a desire from the smaller unions, which is shared by World Rugby, for the Nations Cup commercial rights to be bundled with and sold alongside those of the Nations Championship, which would give them a right to a share of the proceeds.

While the Nations Championship has secured more than 80 broadcast deals for this year’s tournament in deals that were brokered before F10 was set up, the Nations Cup has brought in just 13, with games streamed on the World Rugby-owned RugbyPass TV in many markets, including the UK.

articles.title: Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja's autobiography has exposed the limbo Australian cricket finds itself stuck in over the sandpaper scandal, writes Stephan Shemilt.
body: There are stories that can damage reputations, tarnish legacies and put asterisks next to achievements.

Are Pep Guardiola's trophies at Manchester City rendered worthless by financial rule breaches? Would either of the Houston Astros or Boston Red Sox have won the World Series without sign stealing? How much fake blood was spilled by Harlequins?

Now, sandpapergate has morphed into Usman Khawaja's-book-gate, opening old wounds and asking questions that have hung over Australian cricket since Cameron Bancroft hid some DIY equipment in his jockstrap in 2018.
Published on Tuesday, Khawaja's autobiography – Sabr – is only suggesting what plenty have suspected for the past eight years.

articles.title: F1 planning to finish season in Middle East as Imola deadline passes
articles.summary: Formula 1 chiefs are proceeding with plans to hold the final two rounds of 2026 in the Middle East after a deadline to move one of the season-ending races to Italy passed.
body: F1 had to cancel races scheduled in April in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia due to conflict in the Middle East, which has continued throughout the year to cast doubt over the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

A contingency plan had been arranged for Imola to host a season-ending race in the first week of December, but those in charge at the Italian circuit were informed on Tuesday that it will not be needed, which confirms F1's intention to go ahead with the final two rounds as planned.

The Qatar Grand Prix is scheduled for November 27-29, with the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix set to follow from December 4-6. The races complete a triple-header that starts with the Las Vegas Grand Prix from November 20-22.
F1 president Stefano Domenicali has maintained throughout the season that the final races would be held at their scheduled venues unless the situation in the Middle East deteriorated.

Joint-trainers John and Thady Gosden elected against a Breeders' Cup run for the son of Night Of Thunder after his victory in the Champion Stakes, but he will now tackle a mile and a half for the first time in Tokyo on November 29 before stallion duties await at Darley's Kildangan Stud in Ireland in 2027.

However, win, lose or draw in the Far East, Godolphin's managing director Hugh Anderson believes his legacy has already been secured and he will go down as "one of the best" to represent Sheikh Mohammed's operation on the racetrack.
He told the Press Association: "John is a master trainer and has obviously got his eye very firmly on this prize. It's very exciting.

articles.title: Conference championships were maddening, and I’ll miss them anyway
articles.summary: Conference championship games were flawed, frustrating and sometimes downright unfair, but college football won't be quite the same without them.
body: Farewell, conference championships. You were inspiring and infuriating, often irrelevant and occasionally actively harmful. You were born out of sheer profit motive, and you died the same way.

The Power 4 conference championships, which end after this season, are an understandable victim of the expansion to a 24-team playoff, an easy sacrifice with few defenders. The college football powers-that-be officially sent them to a farm upstate on Monday, but they’d been obsolete for years.

Implemented — like so much else in college football — in haphazard fashion, the conference championships represented the imbalance inherent in the sport. The SEC’s version dates to 1992; the Big Ten didn’t get around to staging one until 2011. Notre Dame, as an independent, managed to sidestep the annual early-December schedule land mine by simply declining to participate in one. Turns out in college football, you can just … do things like that.

articles.title: Merson: Man Utd transfer policy is to blame - not Carrick
articles.summary: Sky Sports' Paul Merson believes Manchester United’s transfer strategy is to blame for their worst start to a top-flight season instead of head coach Michael Carrick.
body: Carrick's job is increasingly in doubt, with United sitting in the Premier League relegation zone after taking only eight points from their first 10 games, and Mauricio Pochettino is open to a discussion if approached.

One win in 11 games, 30 goals conceded in all competitions, the worst record of any team in the top-five European leagues and a club-worst start to a league season has ramped up the pressure on Carrick - but Merson feels he is not at fault.
"I just can't blame the manager. They change managers left, right and centre all the time and it's the same results," said Merson.
"It doesn't matter if you have Arsene Wenger, Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola or Jose Mourinho sitting on the bench. The mistakes they are making are down to the players.

articles.title: NHL rumors: Will Hockey Hall of Fame waive 3-year waiting period for Alex Oveckin?
articles.summary: appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The greatest goal scorer in NHL history will be calling it a career this year, as Alex Ovechkin has announced this will be his final season in the NHL.
body: Ovechkin and the Capitals hope that he will get to lift the Stanley Cup one more time before his career ends. Regardless of the outcome of this season, the greatest goal scorer of all time will be heading to Toronto for induction into the Hockey Hall of Fame at some point down the road. The biggest question is: when will it happen? Traditionally, players have to wait three years to be eligible, but there is the possibility that the Hall of Fame could waive the waiting period, something Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic explored.

“And Alex Ovechkin? He has announced this will be his final NHL season, and some have wondered if the Hockey Hall of Fame should waive its three-year waiting period for the all-time NHL goals leader, as it did for players like Gordie Howe, Mario Lemieux and Wayne Gretzky,” LeBrun wrote.

Howe, Lemieux, and Gretzky are clearly three of the best to ever play the game. They did not have to wait to be enshrined in the Hall of Fame. Still, LeBrun does not think that Ovi will be given the same opportunity.

In a video shared on X/Twitter, he said: “We would play in any weather and we were challenged every day to be our best, too. And I think that’s maybe what the modern athletes [are] really missing.
“Who’s challenging those kids to be their very best? Not who’s paying for their lunch money that day or who’s paying for the sponsorship.
